Fazlul Karim with Md Abdullah, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
Rafiqur Rahman, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No.2
parties:
Harunar Rashid (Md) son of late Rafique Uddin,Jinnath Mahal  ------ Petitioner
vs.  
Subordinate Judge, (Artha Rin Adalat) Bogra and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Qazi Shafiuddin J: A Rule Nisi was issued upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and decree passed by the respondent No.1 in Artha Rin Adalat Suit No.248 of 1991 on 16-7-92 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect 

 2. Short facts for the disposal of the Rule are that the petitioner was appointed as Steno-Typist of Muslim Commercial Bank on 21-6-65. The said Bank along with others was re-named as Rupali Bank under PO No. 26/72. The petitioner was appointed as Manager, Rupali Bank, Shilpa Shaka, Bogra. The respondent No.4 opened a current account in the name of respondent No. 3 showing him as the proprietor of the same and deposited Taka 25,000.00. On 13-8-88 the petitioner was under suspension on various charges stating that he has caused loss to the Bank by distributing loans to different persons without any authority. Thereafter a criminal case was also started on 11-6-89 against the petitioner. The charges leveled against the petitioner were denied by him. He surrendered before the Divisional Special Judge, Rajshahi on 19-5-92 and the prayer for bail was refused but subsequently he was granted bail on 5-8-92 by the High Court Division. The petitioner was released on 16-8-92 from Rajshahi Jail and thereafter he came to know that a decree was passed by respondent No.1 for Taka 11,87,085.00 with interest at the rate of 20% and after collecting necessary information he filed this present application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. In this petition the petitioner has seriously challenged the jurisdiction of the Artha Rin Adalat and submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat had no jurisdiction to entertain such application and pass a decree against the petitioner. It is further stated that during his absence while he was in the Jail hajat the impugned decree was passed behind his back as such principle of natural justice has been violated, It is also submitted that the impugned judgment is violative of the provision of Article 27,31 and 32 of the Constitution as such the same is to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. 

 4. At the outset Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 2 bank submitted that the writ petition is not maintainable inasmuch as the forum by way of an appeal has been created by the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 (Act 4 of 1990) as such without availing that forum this petition is not maintainable. He further submits that the Artha Rin Adalat has committed no illegality in passing the impugned judgment and decree. He further submits that the petitioner has misappropriated the money and the same is nothing but a debt. 

 It is stated that respondent No.2 i.e. the bank filed a Suit being No. 248/91 stating that respondent No.4 opened current account No.868 on 19.4.88 as the proprietor of respondent No.3 and deposited Taka 25,000.00. Respondent No.4 in between 21-4-88 to 25-4-88 overdrew Taka 3,35,00.00. The said respondent deposited Taka 12,000.00 on 26-4-88 but over-drew Taka 4,03,000.00 on 27-4-88. Altogether he has withdrawn Taka 85,000.00 on that date. On 31-7-88 respondent No.4 deposited Taka 6,84,775.00 and on 1-8-88 he had withdrawn the entire amount and thus had withdrawn an excess amount of Taka 6,84,755.00. It is alleged in the plaint that respondent No.4 operated the said account on advice and in collusion with the petitioner Md. Harunar Rashid. It is further stated in the said plaint that the respondent No.4 was asked to adjust the account on payment of money due as aforesaid. The respondent No.4 stated that the petitioner while at the bank has used his cheque to withdraw Taka 7,00,000.00 from the aforesaid account for his own purpose and to that effect the petitioner had already sworn an affidavit before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Bogra stating that he would pay off the said amount with interest and the respondent No.2 prayed for a decree of Taka 11,87,085.00 with interest at the rate of 20% till the date of realisation from the petitioner. In fact that said amount has been decreed by the Artha Rin Adalat. In the judgment Annexure-D to the petitioner it was held that the petitioner Harunar Rashid had obtained the amount by practicing fraud and forgery as such the same is recoverable and accordingly the Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit. 

 Furthermore it has been stated in the preamble of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 that the Artha Rin Adalat Act is a Special legislation to realise the loan given by the financial institution. The Adalat Act is a special ligislation providing for special measures to realise the loans given by financial institutions. Section 5(1) of the Act provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law all suits concerning the realisation of "loan" by financial institutions shall be instituted in the Artha Rin Adalat and all such suits shall be decided only in the said Adalat. The clear implication of section 5(1) read with section 2(Kha) of the Adalat Act is, that it is only a financial institution which can be a plaintiff before the Artha Rin Adalat and no one else. It also implies that all kinds of suits are not entertainable by the Artha Rin Adalat. Only those suits which are concerned with the realisation of "loan" as defined in the Act and is disbursed by a financial institution can be filed in the Artha Rin Adalat, no other kind of suit is entertainable, (Ref: 46 DLR (AD) 174). As we have already observed that the money so obtained by the petitioner does not in any way fall within the definition of section 2(Kha) of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990. The same cannot be treated as 'Rin' as defined in the said Act as such the Artha Rin Adalat travelled beyond their jurisdiction to entertain such suit. The Artha Rin Adalat has been specially established for deciding those cases only which are for recovery of the loan advanced by the financial institution. The learned Artha Rin Adalat has acted absolutely without jurisdiction as no power has been vested in the Artha Rin Adalat to try a case other than the realisation of loan money. Furthermore the Artha Rin Adalat has committed a serious illegality in coming to a conclusion that the petitioner has already obtained the amount by practicing fraud, forgery and in deceitful manner when a criminal case was in progress and the petitioner was in Jail hajat, the Artha Rin Adalat should not have entertained such suit without any clear materials that the money in question did constitute a loan money. A stolen goods cannot be a subject matter for decision by a Artha Rin Adalat. Loan must be advanced by the financial institution and must be accepted by the loanee. Therefore the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat appears to have been passed without any lawful authority. When the action complained of is purely without jurisdiction, submission by way of appeal is inefficacious and redundant. 

 6. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Suit No. 248/91 on 16-7-92 (Annexure-D to the petition) is hereby declared to have been passed or made without any lawful authority and to be of no legal affect.
